name: Differentiable Rendering
text:
# Differentiable Rendering

Also called: Differentiable Splatting, Gradient-Based Rendering

## Overview
Differentiable rendering treats the image formation process as a differentiable function, enabling the computation of gradients with respect to scene parameters (geometry, appearance, pose) via backpropagation [G]. This allows for gradient-based optimization of 3D representations directly from 2D image observations [G]. It sets itself apart from standard rendering by exposing internal state gradients to upstream optimizers, facilitating tasks like pose estimation, shape reconstruction, and sequential affordance reasoning for robotic planning [S1, unofficial][S2]. It builds on [Splatting](23-splatting.md) by differentiating the [rasterization](#15310-rasterization.md) and [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) steps.

## Subtopics

### [Differentiable Forward Warping with Average Splatting](8921-differentiable-forward-warping-with-average-splatting.md)
Solves the "many-to-one" mapping issue in temporal deformation by fusing source voxel values into a target grid using trilinear kernel weights, addressing density collisions during contraction.

### [Learning and Training Methods](9068-learning-and-training-methods.md)
Focuses on optimizing primitive parameters and network weights through differentiable rendering pipelines to learn 3D representations from 2D images [G].

### [Differentiable Robot Rendering (Dr. Robot)](15698-differentiable-robot-rendering-dr-robot.md)
Integrates kinematics-aware deformation with 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) using Implicit Linear Blend Skinning (LBS) to provide accurate gradients for robotic control and planning.

### SeqAffordSplat
Performs sequential affordance reasoning on the [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) representation, where rendered [feature fields](#12995-feature-fields.md) encode [interaction](#41-interaction.md) probabilities over time, allowing robots to plan actions in the rendered 3D scene [S1, unofficial].

### Differentiable Rendering (Forward Pass)
For Fourier [splatting](#23-splatting.md), the forward pass implements a [tile-based rasterizer](#2846-tile-based-rasteriser.md) in polar coordinates [S2]. For each pixel $j$ with polar coordinates $(\rho_j, \theta_j)$ in the tangent plane of primitive $s_i$, the signed distance to the boundary is computed as $\varphi_j = \rho_j - r_i(\theta_j)$ [S2]. Points with $\varphi_j \ge 0$ are discarded [S2]. The per-pixel opacity is calculated as $\alpha_{i,j} = o_i \cdot \max\left(0, \frac{r_i(\theta_j) - \rho_j}{r_i(\theta_j)}\right)^{\sigma_i}$ [S2]. Colors are accumulated via front-to-back compositing [S2].

## Background
Differentiable rendering has evolved from volume rendering techniques to support modern neural graphics [G]. Early work focused on [volume rendering equations](#2098-volume-rendering-equation.md), where opacity $\alpha$ is computed by integrating density along the ray: $\alpha_i = 1 - \exp\left(-\int G_i(x) dx\right)$ [S1, unofficial]. Recent advancements integrate these principles with Gaussian Splatting, enabling applications like robot learning and 3D reconstruction [S1, unofficial][S2]. Fourier Splatting extends this by using generalized [Fourier encoded primitives](#11094-fourier-splatting-primitive.md), adapting power window functions to polar coordinates for scalable radiance fields [S2].
